## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 78, entitled *Upassuti* ("Eavesdropping"), belongs to the Vinaya Piṭaka of the Pali Canon. The rule provides that a monk who eavesdrops on other monastics when they are disputing matters concerning the Teaching or monastic law incurs an offense requiring confession. An English translation of the text is available by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within Pali literature, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Pācittiya 78, Bhikkhu Parivāra Pācittiya 78, and the parallel nun's rule found in Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, Pātimokkha, and Parivāra Pācittiya 156. Parallels are also extant in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan versions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinaya lineages.

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus reflects extensive formulaic reuse within the Pali Vinaya, showing substantial shared segments with other Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rules—including Pācittiya 23, 76, 77, 75, and 55—as well as the sub-commentarial *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with non-Pali monastic treatises, such as the Tibetan translations of the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007), *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120), and *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105), as well as Jayarakṣita's Sanskrit *Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
